newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ can't up rates until some firms recover - report.
newsitem.headline: BOJ can't up rates until some firms recover - report.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will not be able to raise interest rates because of weakness in Japanese non-manufacturers and small- and medium-sized manufacturers, Kokusai Securities Co said in a report on Wednesday.
It said Japan's major manufacturers were the only ones showing signs of recovering, and added that under such a "two-tier" economy, the effects of monetary policy would greatly diminish.
The profitability of non-manufacturers and small- and medium-sized manufacturers remains low and in light of such conditions, a credit tightening is unlikely, the report said.

"The profitability of non-manufacturers and medium- to smaller-size manufacturers has barely improved in the past three years. Their weakness makes it hard to believe that we are experiencing an economic recovery," Kokusai said.
"If the 'gradual' recovery was evenly spread out among most sectors of the economy, then the (BOJ's) 'super' low interest rate policy would have been corrected already," it added.
Currently, most of the profits at non-manufacturers arise from a decrease in interest rate payments, so a credit tightening will only eat away at their profits, it said.
"Non-manufacturers make up 60 to 70 percent of the overall economy and a correction to the 'super' low interest rate policy has become difficult," the report added.

The second-tier brokerage firm said structural reforms, including cutting personnel costs, were necessary for an improvement in business conditions at non-manufacturers, but it would also bring about a drop in income.
It also did not elaborate when the BOJ would be able to raise interest rates.
